memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Now Israel loved Joseph more than any of his other sons, because he had been born to him in his old age; and he made an ornate robe for him. When his brothers saw that their father loved him more than any of them, they hated him and could not speak a kind word to him." - Gen 37:3-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Jacob "loved Joseph more than any of his other sons," and he made no secret of it. He gave Joseph a special ornate robe — a visible, daily reminder to the other brothers that Joseph was the favorite. The result was a home poisoned by resentment: the brothers "hated him and could not speak a kind word to him."

Jacob, of all people, should have known where favoritism leads. He had grown up in a home split by it, his father preferring Esau and his mother preferring him (Gen 25:28). That partiality had torn his family apart. Now he repeats the very same wound with his own children. Sadly, we often pass on the very hurts we suffered, unless we let God break the cycle.

Favoritism is quietly destructive. Whenever we treat some people as more valued than others — in a family, a friendship, a church, a workplace — we sow seeds of jealousy and division. God Himself "does not show favoritism" (Rom 2:11), and He calls us to love without partiality (Jas 2:1).

Look honestly at your relationships. Is there a "robe" you are giving to one person that quietly wounds another? Ask God to help you love the people around you fairly and fully, so your home does not grow the bitter fruit we see here.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where might I be showing partiality that wounds others?
2. Am I repeating a hurtful pattern I once suffered myself?
3. How can I love those around me more fairly and fully?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You show no favoritism. Guard my heart from partiality, and help me to love those around me fairly. Break in me any harmful pattern I have inherited. Amen.
